title: Cosimplicial coend adjunction and its canonical homotopy-colimit counit
statement:
Use the universes of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the complete, cocomplete model-category, weak-equivalence, cofibrant-object and Reedy terminology of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. A cosimplicial resolution means a Reedy cofibrant functor $A^\bullet:\Delta\to\mathcal M$ whose structure maps are weak equivalences. Its canonical augmentation to $\operatorname{const}(A^0)$ is induced by the unique maps $[n]\to[0]$. Use homotopy colimits of [lem-coef-hocolim-reindexing-zigzags], computed by the colimit of a projectively cofibrant replacement. Let $\mathcal M$ be combinatorial, $D$ small, and $A:D\to\mathcal M^\Delta$ a functor with cosimplicial-resolution values. Give $\mathsf U(D)=\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{sSet})$ the projective model structure of [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model]. There is a Quillen adjunction $L_A:\mathsf U(D)\rightleftarrows\mathcal M:R_A$ with
$$(R_AX)(d)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(A_d^n,X),\qquad L_AF=\int^{d\in D}\int^{[n]\in\Delta} A_d^n\cdot F(d)_n.$$
Here $Z\cdot S=\coprod_{s\in S}Z$, and each coend is the coproduct of the indicated terms modulo the relations induced by the arrows of the indexing category. The counit is induced by evaluation $A_d^n\to X$. For a fibrant $X$ and every projective cofibrant replacement $q:Q R_AX\to R_AX$, the arrow $\varepsilon_X L_Aq:L_AQ R_AX\to X$ is isomorphic in the slice $\operatorname{Ho}(\mathcal M)/X$ to the canonical arrow $\operatorname{hocolim}_{K_X}T_X\to X$. Here $K_X$ has objects $(d,[n],u:A_d^n\to X)$, arrows $(a,\alpha):(d,[n],u)\to(e,[m],u')$ with $a:d\to e$, $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$ satisfying $u'A_e(\alpha)A_a^n=u$, and $T_X(d,[n],u)=A_d^n$, $T_X(a,\alpha)=A_e(\alpha)A_a^n$; the canonical arrow is induced by the cocone of the maps $u$. In particular, for every such $q$ the counit composite is a weak equivalence exactly when this canonical homotopy-colimit augmentation is a weak equivalence. No density or generation assumption on $A$ is made.

proof.text: By the Reedy model-structure statement, every value of each Reedy cofibrant resolution $A_d^\bullet$ is cofibrant, and its latching map $L_nA_d\to A_d^n$ is a cofibration. For fixed $d$ put $V_d(K)=\int^{[n]\in\Delta}A_d^n\cdot K_n$. Maps out of the coend are compatible families of maps from its summands; this gives the right adjoint $X\mapsto(n\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(A_d^n,X))$, so $V_d$ preserves colimits. The coend formula gives $V_d(\Delta^n)=A_d^n$ and $V_d(\partial\Delta^n)=L_nA_d$; it also identifies the map $V_d(\Delta^n)\to V_d(\Delta^0)$ with the canonical collapse $A_d^n\to A_d^0$. These maps are respectively cofibrations and weak equivalences by the resolution hypotheses. The boundary-collapse criterion therefore makes $V_d$ a left Quillen functor, with the right adjoint just described.

source.place: Proposition 4.2 and Corollary 4.4, printed pp. 184-185; Dugger Universal Homotopy Theories Proposition 3.4, printed p. 154

proof.text: For $h_d\times K$, the $D$-coend collapses by the Yoneda relation: the summand indexed by $a:e\to d$ maps using $A_a$, and the inverse uses $1_d$. Hence $L_A(h_d\times K)=V_d(K)$, naturally in $d,K$. Maps $L_AF\to X$ are compatible families of functions $F(d)_n\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(A_d^n,X)$, so are precisely maps $F\to R_AX$. This proves the adjunction and identifies its counit with evaluation. To check Quillenness without an implicit closure argument, let $p$ be a fibration (respectively trivial fibration) in $\mathcal M$. A lifting problem for $(R_Ap)(d)$ against a horn (respectively boundary) is adjoint to one for $p$ against the image of that inclusion under $V_d$. Step 1 makes that image a trivial cofibration (respectively cofibration), so a lift exists. The generating-family characterization in the projective-model node now makes $R_Ap$ a projective fibration (respectively trivial fibration), proving that $L_A\dashv R_A$ is Quillen.

For a simplicial presheaf $F$ let $E_F$ and $B_F$ be the category and representable-simplex diagram in the cited resolution statement. Under the coend calculation in Step 2, $L_AB_F(d,[n],\sigma)=A_d^n$, and the arrow $(a:d\to e,\alpha:[n]\to[m])$ acts by $A_e(\alpha)A_a^n$. Put $T_F=L_AB_F$. For $F=R_AX$, a simplex $\sigma$ is exactly a map $u:A_d^n\to X$. Its arrow equation becomes $u' A_e(\alpha)A_a^n=u$. Thus $E_{R_AX}=K_X$ and $T_{R_AX}=T_X$, as categories and diagrams, with matching evaluation cocones.

source.place: Section 9.5, printed pp. 171-172; explicit category-of-simplices identification

proof.text: Choose a projectively cofibrant replacement $P B_F\to B_F$ and put $H_F=\operatorname{colim}P B_F$. The representable-simplex resolution theorem gives that $H_F$ is cofibrant in $\mathsf U(D)$ and its evaluation augmentation $e_F:H_F\to F$ is a weak equivalence. The projective diagram model structure exists because $\mathsf U(D)$ is combinatorial by the projective-model statement. This applies to arbitrary $F$, including $F=R_AX$, without using fibrancy.

source.place: Proposition 2.9, printed p. 152; proof Section 9.1, printed pp. 170-171

proof.text: Write $\mathbf L L_A$ and $\mathbf R R_A$ for the derived adjunction supplied by the model-category derived-adjunction statement. The model-colimit comparison identifies $H_F$ with the coherent colimit of $B_F$ after localization. Each $h_d\times\Delta^n$ is projectively cofibrant: its initial map is the image of the cofibration $\varnothing\to\Delta^n$ under the left adjoint to evaluation, whose right adjoint is objectwise right Quillen. Thus $\mathbf L L_A(B_F(d,[n],\sigma))$ is represented by $A_d^n$, and, since $H_F$ is cofibrant, $\mathbf L L_A(H_F)$ is represented by $L_AH_F$. Here is the required preservation of this colimit, with its cocone: for every localized target $Y$, derived adjunction and the colimit universal property give $\operatorname{Map}(\mathbf L L_A(H_F),Y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(H_F,\mathbf R R_A(Y))\simeq\lim_{E_F^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}(B_F(-),\mathbf R R_A(Y))\simeq\lim_{E_F^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}(T_F(-),Y)$. These equivalences send restriction along each coprojection to restriction along the corresponding coprojection, by naturality of adjunction. Consequently $L_AH_F$ with its induced cocone represents the colimit of $T_F$. The model-colimit statement identifies that same colimit with $\operatorname{hocolim}_{E_F}T_F$. The equivalence therefore respects each cocone map, including the cocone to $X$ when $F=R_AX$.

source.place: Proposition 4.2 proof, printed pp. 184-185: apply the left Quillen realization to the representable-simplex homotopy-colimit resolution; preservation is expanded via the derived mapping-space adjunction.

proof.text: Now fix fibrant $X$, put $F=R_AX$, and take the specified projective cofibrant replacement $q:QF\to F$. The argument uses only that $q$ is a weak equivalence with cofibrant source, so it covers a trivial-fibration replacement as a special case. Factor $(e_F,q):H_F\amalg QF\to F$ by the model factorization as a cofibration followed by a trivial fibration $p:C\to F$, and write $i:H_F\to C$, $j:QF\to C$ for the two components, so $pi=e_F$ and $pj=q$. The coproduct of the cofibrant objects $H_F$ and $QF$ is cofibrant (its initial map is a pushout of the two initial cofibrations), so $C$ is cofibrant. Since $p$, $e_F$ and $q$ are weak equivalences, two-out-of-three makes $i$ and $j$ weak equivalences between cofibrant objects; the derived-adjunction statement says $L_Ai$ and $L_Aj$ are weak equivalences. After applying evaluation we have the strict equalities $(\varepsilon_XL_Ap)L_Ai=\varepsilon_XL_Ae_F$ and $(\varepsilon_XL_Ap)L_Aj=\varepsilon_XL_Aq$. The augmentation $e_F$ comes from the composite cocone $P B_F\to B_F\to F$. After applying $L_A$ and evaluation, its component on the original object $L_AB_F(d,[n],u)=A_d^n$ is exactly $u:A_d^n\to X$; the cocone on $L_AP B_F$ is obtained by precomposition. Since $X$ is fibrant, the derived-adjunction statement identifies this evaluation with the derived counit, without an additional fibrant replacement of $X$. Step 5 therefore identifies the arrow $\varepsilon_XL_Ae_F:L_AH_F\to X$ with the canonical homotopy-colimit augmentation, and the weak equivalences $L_Ai$, $L_Aj$ over $X$ identify it with $\varepsilon_XL_Ap$ and then with the specified counit composite $\varepsilon_XL_Aq$ in $\operatorname{Ho}(\mathcal M)/X$. This proves the slice comparison for every $q$, rather than only for one chosen resolution.

source.place: Proposition 4.2 and Corollary 4.4, printed pp. 184-185; the factorization comparing arbitrary cofibrant approximations and the evaluation equation make the slice compatibility explicit.

proof.text: Finally, the model-category localization detects weak equivalences: a morphism is a weak equivalence exactly when its image in the ordinary localization is an isomorphism. Isomorphic arrows in the slice have simultaneously invertible images, so the counit composite is a weak equivalence exactly when the canonical homotopy-colimit augmentation is one. The argument uses no density or generation property of $A$; only the Reedy resolution hypotheses and the projective cofibrant replacement were used.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 4.2 and Corollary 4.4, printed pp. 184-185; coend pair from Universal Homotopy Theories Proposition 3.4 / Section 9.5, printed pp. 154, 171-172. Uses its Proposition 2.9, printed p. 152 and proof pp. 170-171, for the representable-simplex resolution. Left Quillen preservation of that colimit and slice compatibility are expanded in Steps 5-6.

lean.note: Uses the already landed ProjectiveFrame.mappingFunctor and IsCoend (the added statement dependency) for the actual Hom presheaf and full double-coend universal property. The unit gives the coend coprojections; an explicit evaluation equation fixes the counit. CostructuredArrow supplies the exact canonical simplex index, and the colimit of any specified projective replacement supplies its canonical augmentation. The comparison is an isomorphism in the slice of the ordinary localization, for every cofibrant weak-equivalence approximation, including approximations which are not fibrations.
